title: All aboard the cervical screening bus: how NHS clinic-on-wheels is saving lives

paragraphs.en: It’s 10am on one of the main pedestrian shopping streets in Warrington, and already there’s a queue of women outside a small bus the size of a supermarket delivery van. While some look calm, others are visibly nervous. This is no mobile library, post office or coffee truck – but one providing far more intimate services: cervical screening.
paragraphs.zh: 上午10点，在沃灵顿一条主要的步行购物街上，一辆只有超市送货车大小的小巴士外已经排起了女性长队。有些人看上去很平静，另一些人则明显紧张不安。这不是流动图书馆、流动邮局或咖啡车，而是一辆提供更为私密服务的车：宫颈癌筛查。

paragraphs.en: The bus feels surprisingly spacious. There’s a consultation area with room for the nurses, patients and anyone accompanying them to talk. Behind it, a separate room holds a bed, room to get changed and storage for all the clinical equipment. Purple lighting, smart decor and spa music add to the minimalist ambience.
paragraphs.zh: 这辆巴士令人意外地宽敞。有一个咨询区，护士、患者及其陪同人员可以在这里交谈。后面还有一间单独的房间，里面有床、更衣空间以及存放所有临床设备的柜子。紫色灯光、精致的装饰和舒缓的音乐营造出极简的氛围。

paragraphs.en: Catherine, 26, is the first in the queue. She has never had cervical screening before. She says the fact that it is a bus, with people she doesn’t know, persuaded her to go ahead with it. “I didn’t go for screening before because there’s only one nurse at my doctor’s and she’s my asthma nurse,” Catherine says. “So it felt too familiar.”
paragraphs.zh: 26岁的凯瑟琳排在队伍最前面。她以前从未做过宫颈癌筛查。她说，正因为这是一辆巴士、里面是不认识的人，才促使她决定来做检查。“我以前没来做筛查，是因为我的医生那里只有一名护士，而她是我的哮喘专科护士，”凯瑟琳说。“所以感觉太熟了。”

paragraphs.en: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer in women, according to the World Health Organization . Its cervical cancer strategy states that by 2030 all countries should screen 70% of girls and vaccinate 90% of girls by the age of 15.
paragraphs.zh: 根据世界卫生组织的数据，宫颈癌是女性第四大常见癌症。世卫组织的宫颈癌战略规定，到2030年，所有国家都应让70%的女孩接受筛查，并在15岁前为90%的女孩接种疫苗。

paragraphs.en: But NHS figures show there are just over 4 million women in England who are not up to date with their cervical screening, and that number is rising. According to OECD data , in the decade since 2014, screening rates in England have fallen eight percentage points to 69%, the fourth steepest drop behind Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Turkey.
paragraphs.zh: 但英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）的数据显示，英格兰有400多万名女性未及时接受宫颈癌筛查，而且这一数字还在上升。根据经合组织（OECD）的数据，自2014年以来的十年间，英格兰的筛查率下降了8个百分点，降至69%，降幅在卢森堡、荷兰和土耳其之后位列第四。

paragraphs.en: According to the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, women from ethnic minority backgrounds, disabled women, LGBTQ+ people with a cervix, and those in deprived areas are less likely to be up to date with screening.
paragraphs.zh: 根据英国皇家妇产科学院的说法，少数族裔背景的女性、残疾女性、有宫颈的LGBTQ+人群以及贫困地区的女性，更有可能未及时接受筛查。

paragraphs.en: In 2024, in a move to improve take up, Living Well buses started running walk-in cervical screening clinics in Cheshire and Merseyside. Funded by NHS England North West, the service was so popular that this summer it expanded into neighbouring regions. Now, two buses run 10 cervical screening sessions a week across Lancashire and South Cumbria, as well as Cheshire and Merseyside. From October, the service will start going to locations in Greater Manchester.
paragraphs.zh: 2024年，为提高筛查参与率，“健康生活”流动巴士开始在英国柴郡和默西塞德郡开设免预约宫颈癌筛查诊所。该服务由英格兰西北部NHS资助，广受欢迎，今年夏天已扩展至邻近地区。目前，有两辆巴士每周在兰开夏郡、南坎布里亚郡以及柴郡和默西塞德郡开展10场宫颈癌筛查活动。从10月起，该服务将开始前往大曼彻斯特地区的各个地点。

paragraphs.en: Jill West, one of the nurses running the clinic, says mobile screening is game-changing. “The bus is fantastic. Women can sometimes forget about their own health – they’ve got children to think about, work to think about, they can’t get a convenient GP appointment, or fit it in with their menstrual cycle. So the bus is perfect because it’s advertised and women can come along and get screened without having to make an appointment.”
paragraphs.zh: 负责运营该诊所的护士之一吉尔·韦斯特（Jill West）表示，流动筛查具有变革意义。“这辆巴士太棒了。女性有时会忘记自己的健康——她们要想着孩子、想着工作，约不到方便的全科医生门诊，或者难以配合自己的月经周期安排时间。所以这辆巴士非常完美，因为它有宣传，女性可以随时来接受筛查，无需预约。”
